info.title: Ledgerbase API
info.description:
OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the Ledgerbase Flask service. Documents the currently exposed routes and the cross-cutting error responses produced by the registered Flask error handlers.

All documented endpoints (`/`, `/debug-sentry`, `/login`) are intentionally public diagnostic / liveness routes; no authentication is required. The previous `ApiKeyAuth` scheme was removed since no operation enforced it. Future production endpoints will be documented under `components.securitySchemes` and reference an explicit `security` block.

Content negotiation: the registered error handlers in `src/ledgerbase/error_handlers.py` return the JSON envelopes documented below only when the client sends `Accept: application/json`. With any other Accept header the handlers render the corresponding HTML template (`404.html`, `422.html`, `500.html`); reusable error responses below model both content types. API clients should send `Accept: application/json` to receive the JSON form.

Monetary amounts are always serialized as JSON strings (never numbers) to preserve Decimal precision. The reusable `MonetaryAmount` schema component (type: string, format: decimal) is provided for future endpoints that accept or return monetary values.

get.description: Returns a plain text greeting confirming the Ledgerbase API process is running. Used as a lightweight liveness/health check.

Internal diagnostic route. Deliberately raises a `ZeroDivisionError` to verify Sentry error-monitoring wiring; always responds 500. This endpoint is documented here because it is registered on the Flask app, but it is not part of the public API contract — production deployments should either restrict it (authentication / network policy) or disable it via a feature flag. Do not depend on this path from client code.
Stub login endpoint protected by a 5-requests-per-minute rate limit. Returns a placeholder confirmation string. Returns 429 Too Many Requests when the limiter threshold is exceeded.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (more than 5 requests per minute). The default Flask-Limiter handler returns the werkzeug TooManyRequests HTML page; no custom JSON error handler is registered for 429.

MonetaryAmount.description: A monetary amount serialized as a string to preserve Decimal precision. Never represented as a JSON number. Example: "123.45".

Error.description: Generic error response body used by the 404 and 500 error handlers.

ValidationError.description: Validation error response body produced by the marshmallow ValidationError handler.

errors.description: Field-keyed map of validation error messages.

NotFound.description: Resource not found. Returned by the registered 404 handler in `src/ledgerbase/error_handlers.py` as JSON for `Accept: application/json` and as the `404.html` template for any other Accept header.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Request body failed marshmallow validation. Returned by the registered 422 handler as JSON for `Accept: application/json` and as the `422.html` template for any other Accept header.

schema.description: Rendered `422.html` template (receives the marshmallow error map as `errors`).

InternalServerError.description: Unhandled server error. Returned by the registered 500 handler as JSON for `Accept: application/json` and as the `500.html` template for any other Accept header.
